details: Partial equivalence queries include both total equivalence and one-point membership queries.
proof: An arbitrary equivalence query is a total partial equivalence query, and a membership query is a partial query defined at one point. Thus partial equivalence queries include every query available in the membership-and-equivalence model.
name: Membership and Equivalence Queries Complexity / Partial Equivalence Queries Complexity
witness_verification: On $\mathrm{ADDRESSING}_n$, a partial hypothesis which labels every address point negative identifies the target after its unique counterexample, so $\mathrm{LC}_{\mathrm{partial}}=1$.  Maass--Turán prove $\mathrm{LC}_{\mathrm{ARB\text{-}MEMB}}=\Theta(\log n)$ for the same family.  Thus the gap is unbounded.
